jobs.title: Managing Director - Capital Advisory
jobs.description:
About Vortex Capital:

Vortex Capital is a boutique capital advisory firm with a strong track record and extensive capabilities, having advised on over 500 billion in transaction volume across our team members & advisors. With a presence in major global hubs, including Zurich, London, New York, Miami, and Vancouver, we deliver value for clients across the early to middle market.

We’re hiring an MD focused on the capital raising and M&A side of our team. We have top-tier deal flow and no shortage of mandates / opportunities to raise for.

Position Overview

The MD will be responsible for leading capital-raising and select sell-side M&A transactions, engaging investors, speaking with clients, and driving successful deal closures. This is a senior role within the firm, working closely with other team members, clients, and investors to ensure seamless execution. Success in this position is measured by the ability to drive transactions to completion, secure investor commitments, and enhance the firm’s market position through exceptional execution and select origination.

Qualifications & Experience:

Licensed under FINRA
Experience raising $10M–$200M+ tickets for sectors like biotech, AI, infrastructure, technology, industrials, or other specialised industries
Proven track record raising from family offices, HNWIs, VCs, and growth equity investors for private companies
7+ years in IB, PE, or VC
Deep investor relationships and strong execution capabilities

Benefits:
Work alongside a top-tier global team of finance professionals with deep sector expertise
Fast growth trajectory with potential to move into partner-level roles quickly
Access to extremely strong deal flow
High earning potential with uncapped high upside tied to deal success

jobs.title: Executive Director, Performing Arts
jobs.description:
Coalition for African Americans in the Performing Arts (CAAPA)

Position - Executive Director, Performing Arts

Job Description

Reports to:
Board of Directors
Supervises
: Staff, contractors, consultants, and volunteers, as applicable
Classification:
Exempt (W-2)

Position Overview

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive and cultural leader of CAAPA, ensuring both artistic excellence and organizational sustainability. This individual will be a passionate advocate for African American performing arts and will work closely with artists, educators, community leaders, donors, and the Board to expand CAAPA's impact through music, performance, arts education, and cultural programming. CAAPA's programs include music and choral performance, youth arts education, cultural heritage programming, artist development, and community engagement initiatives. 

This position requires substantive professional experience in the music, choral, classical, or performing arts sector.

The Executive Director provides overall leadership for strategy, programming, fundraising, financial stewardship, organizational development, community partnerships, and external relations. The Executive Director ensures that CAAPA operates with strong governance, sound financial management, and measurable impact while positioning the organization for sustainable long-term growth.

Success in this role is measured by organizational impact, financial sustainability, strategic execution, and strong relationships with artists, educators, donors, partners, and the Board.

For more information about CAAPA, visit https://4caapa.org

Primary Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

• Lead the creation and implementation of CAAPA's strategic vision and annual operating plan.
• Work closely with the Board to establish priorities, evaluate opportunities, and measure organizational performance.
• Identify emerging opportunities that expand CAAPA's impact throughout the region and nationally.
• Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Program Leadership

• Support artistic planning, audience development, and program growth across CAAPA's music, educational, and cultural initiatives.
• Collaborate with artists, musicians, educators, conductors, performers, and artistic partners to maintain high-quality performing arts programming.
• Oversee CAAPA's programs to ensure mission alignment, measurable impact, fiscal responsibility, and organizational sustainability.
• Work with staff and artistic partners to develop programs that balance mission, quality, audience engagement, and financial responsibility.

Fundraising and Advancement

Lead and expand CAAPA's fundraising and advancement efforts by:

• Developing and implementing an annual fundraising strategy.
• Cultivating relationships with major donors, foundations, corporations, and government agencies.
• Working with the Board to strengthen its fundraising capacity.
• Identifying new revenue opportunities and strategic partnerships.
• Ensuring grant development and stewardship.

Financial Leadership

Provide sound financial stewardship by:

• Developing annual budgets with Board approval.
• Monitoring financial performance and cash flow.
• Ensuring appropriate financial controls and reporting.
• Managing resources responsibly to achieve strategic priorities.
• Presenting clear financial information to the Board.

Board Partnership and Governance

• Partner with the Board to support governance, strategic planning, committee operations, policy implementation, and informed decision-making.
• Implement Board policies and priorities.
• Serve as the primary staff liaison to the Board.

Community Engagement

• Serve as CAAPA's chief ambassador and spokesperson, building relationships with artists, musicians, ensembles, educators, community stakeholders, arts organizations, donors, government agencies, and corporate partners while increasing CAAPA’s visibility and community impact.

Organizational Leadership

Lead the organization by:

• Recruiting, developing, and supervising staff, volunteers, and contractors.
• Establishing clear goals and accountability.
• Creating an inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.
• Ensuring compliance with legal, financial, and nonprofit best practices.

Qualifications

Required:

• Seven or more years of progressive leadership experience in performing arts, choral arts, music, cultural arts, arts administration, or closely related nonprofit organizations.
• Knowledge of performing arts programming, artist engagement, audience development, and cultural arts operations.
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
• Demonstrated success leading organizations or major initiatives.
• Experience in fundraising and donor development.
• Strong financial and budget management skills.
• Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
• Commitment to CAAPA's mission.
• Reside in the Washington, DC Metropolitan Area.
• This position is primarily remote, with occasional on-site attendance required for meetings, special events, performances, donor engagements, board meetings, and other mission-critical activities.

Preferred:

• Experience with choral, vocal, instrumental, classical music, theater, dance, or interdisciplinary arts organizations.
• Experience working directly with artists, ensembles, performers, educators, and arts institutions.
• Grant writing and grant management experience.
• Experience working with nonprofit boards.
• Knowledge of arts education and community engagement.
• Existing relationships within the Washington metropolitan arts community and a broad network of arts professionals and organizations nationwide.

Key Competencies

• Strategic leadership
• Fundraising, marketing, and resource development
• Financial management
• Relationship building
• Organizational management
• Board collaboration
• Community engagement
• Written and verbal communication
• Technology literacy 
• Sound judgment and integrity
• Results orientation

Technical Skills

• Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams)
• Budgeting and Financial Reporting
• Grant Management and Compliance Reporting
• QuickBooks or similar accounting software
• Donor/CRM Database Management
• Virtual Collaboration Platforms
• Social Media and Digital Marketing
• Website Content Management Systems

Success Measures

During the first 12–24 months, the Executive Director will:

• Enhance CAAPA's financial sustainability and diversify revenue.
• Deepen engagement with artists, ensembles, arts educators, and cultural organizations throughout the region.
• Increase contributed income from individuals, foundations, corporations, and public sources.
• Expand strategic partnerships that advance CAAPA's mission.
• Maintain high-quality educational and performance programs.
• Build organizational capacity through effective staff leadership and operational systems.
• Advance Board engagement in governance, fundraising, and strategic planning.
• Increase CAAPA's visibility and community impact through effective communications and public leadership.

The Executive Director must effectively balance mission impact, program excellence, fundraising, and revenue generation to ensure CAAPA's long-term sustainability and growth.

Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $60,000 annually.

Benefits:
Ten (10) paid vacation days annually.
Eight (8) paid holidays annually.
Employer health insurance contribution.
SIMPLE IRA employer matching contribution.

Other Compensation: None.

Application Instructions

Applicants must submit a resume. A cover letter is encouraged but optional. For security reasons, CAAPA accepts resumes only in PDF (.pdf) or Microsoft Word (.docx) formats. Resumes submitted in any other format will not be considered.

Pre-Employment Requirements

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and verification of qualifications, employment history, and references.

Equal Opportunity Employer

CAAPA is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diversity, equity, and respect. We encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Summary Of Job Duties:

The Program Director (PD) provides leadership and oversight for the Family Medicine Residency Program in compliance with the ACGME Program Requirements for Family Medicine.

This position serves within the Baptist Health–UAMS Medical Education Program, a partnership between Baptist Health—the largest private health care system in Arkansas—and the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS), the state’s only academic health sciences university. This collaboration combines the academic excellence and research resources of UAMS with Baptist Health’s community-based care model to train compassionate, skilled family physicians who are prepared to meet the evolving health needs of Arkansas and beyond.

The PD ensures the program fosters excellence in patient care, resident education, faculty development, professionalism, diversity, and continuous improvement, consistent with the BH–UAMS mission to develop the next generation of confident, practice-ready physicians committed to primary care and service to their communities.

Qualifications: Required

Board certification in Family Medicine (ABFM or equivalent).
Active, unrestricted medical license.
Minimum of three years of experience as core faculty or in GME leadership.
Demonstrated skills in teaching, administration, and leadership.

Qualifications: Preferred

Prior Program Director or Associate PD experience.
Experience with ACGME accreditation, quality improvement, and scholarly activity.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Administration

Serve as the single, ACGME-approved Program Director responsible for program design, implementation, and quality.
Maintain continuity of leadership and ensure adequate administrative time for program oversight.
Oversee recruitment, selection, evaluation, promotion, and remediation of residents.
Ensure compliance with ACGME requirements, institutional policies, duty hours, and supervision standards.
Submit required data and documentation for ACGME accreditation and institutional reviews. Curriculum & Education Oversight
Develop and maintain a comprehensive curriculum aligned with ACGME Core Competencies.
Ensure appropriate inpatient, outpatient, and community training experiences that provide continuity of care.
Support resident scholarly activity, simulation, and quality improvement projects.
Monitor resident performance outcomes and use data for program evaluation and improvement. Faculty Development & Resources
Recruit and mentor faculty; provide evaluation and professional development.
Ensure faculty meet ACGME qualifications and allocate sufficient time for education and supervision.
Collaborate with institutional leadership to secure adequate administrative, financial, and clinical resources. Quality & Compliance
Lead annual program evaluation and continuous quality improvement efforts.
Address deficiencies and implement action plans promptly.
Promote a professional, inclusive learning environment. Clinical Practice & Role Modeling
Maintain an active clinical practice to model high-quality, compassionate family medicine care.
Demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, and lifelong learning.

Compensation

Competitive compensation package inclusive of a base salary, leadership attachment, clinical incentive potential, commencement bonus and CME stipend

Time & Effort Allocation

50% - GME Administrative (Program Director)
50% - Clinical (Baptist Health Family Medicine NLR)

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
ABOUT KINZMAN

Kinzman is a pre-launch, connection-driven commerce platform built around the principle of Connection Over Competition. Our model is designed to connect consumers, creators, service providers, and relationship-based sales professionals through trusted recommendations, referrals, and shared economic opportunity.

Kinzman has an established founder, technical leadership, and a developing platform and business model. Our next stage is recruiting the founding creator community, building the operational and revenue infrastructure around them, and preparing for market launch.

We are seeking a hands-on founding Chief Operating Officer who can help turn the vision into a disciplined, fundable, and scalable organization.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a founding executive and equity-partner opportunity for an entrepreneurial operator who understands that early-stage leadership requires building before managing.

The COO will work alongside Kinzman’s executive and technical leadership while taking primary ownership of business operations, launch execution, creator recruitment, fundraising support, and organizational development.

The strongest candidate will have meaningful experience in direct selling, network marketing or MLM, affiliate commerce, creator commerce, relationship-based sales, or a closely related business model. This person must understand both the power of community-driven distribution and the importance of building an ethical, sustainable, and compliant organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Translate Kinzman’s vision and business model into clear operational priorities, timelines, and measurable goals

• Develop and execute the strategy for recruiting, onboarding, engaging, and retaining Kinzman’s founding creator community

• Build and lead the initial sales and business-development structure needed to recruit creators, establish partnerships, and generate early revenue

• Build the operational infrastructure needed to support creators, connectors, consumers, sales teams, and strategic partners

• Help develop and execute Kinzman’s fundraising strategy, including investor outreach, strategic partnerships, grant opportunities, pitch materials, and funding conversations

• Design scalable workflows, policies, performance metrics, budgets, reporting systems, and accountability structures

• Lead launch planning, early revenue strategy, resource allocation, and organizational growth

• Recruit, organize, and lead operational and revenue-producing teams as resources become available

• Collaborate closely with technical leadership to ensure the platform supports business priorities, user needs, and operational requirements

• Identify execution risks, ownership gaps, financial needs, and operational barriers before they interfere with growth

• Help build a culture grounded in accountability, transparency, collaboration, ethical leadership, and Connection Over Competition

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

• Senior leadership experience in operations, business development, fundraising, sales, or organizational growth

• Direct experience with network marketing, MLM, direct selling, affiliate marketing, creator commerce, referral-based sales, or community-led growth

• Demonstrated fundraising ability or strong relationships with investors, grantmakers, strategic partners, sponsors, or other funding sources

• Experience building or scaling an early-stage company, startup, sales organization, marketplace, or membership-based business

• Strong financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, revenue-development, and performance-management capabilities

• Ability to create structure, lead people, and execute without established corporate infrastructure

• Strong negotiation, communication, accountability, and cross-functional leadership skills

• The judgment to distinguish sustainable relationship-based commerce from exploitative or poorly structured MLM practices

• Alignment with Kinzman’s mission and willingness to protect the integrity of its people-centered business model

A specific degree is not required. Proven experience, execution ability, professional relationships, leadership judgment, and alignment with Kinzman’s mission will carry greater weight than formal credentials.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

This is a fully remote opportunity with flexible scheduling during Kinzman’s pre-funding stage. The selected candidate may maintain other professional commitments while contributing agreed time, deliverables, and leadership toward defined company milestones.

The opportunity is intended to expand into a more substantial executive commitment as Kinzman secures funding, generates sustainable revenue, and moves into active operations.

COMPENSATION

Kinzman is currently pre-revenue and pre-funding. This is a founding partnership opportunity, not a currently salaried employee position. There is no immediate salary or guaranteed cash compensation.

The selected candidate will be offered a formally negotiated founding-executive compensation structure that may include equity participation and success-contingent deferred cash compensation. Cash compensation will begin only after mutually defined funding or revenue milestones are achieved.

Equity, vesting, deferred compensation, performance expectations, decision-making authority, time commitments, milestones, and exit provisions will be documented in a written agreement following mutual due diligence and professional review.

This opportunity is best suited for an entrepreneurial executive who is financially able to contribute during the building stage and is motivated by meaningful ownership and long-term value creation. It is not appropriate for someone who requires an immediate guaranteed salary.

TO APPLY

Please submit your LinkedIn profile or résumé and briefly address the following:

• Your experience in direct selling, network marketing, MLM, affiliate commerce, creator commerce, or relationship-based sales

• An organization, program, or revenue system you helped build or scale

• Your fundraising experience and measurable results

• Your availability during the pre-funding stage

• Why a remote, flexible, equity-based founding opportunity is appropriate for you at this stage of your career

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
ABOUT KINZMAN

Kinzman is a pre-launch, connection-driven commerce platform built around the principle of Connection Over Competition. Our model is designed to connect consumers, creators, service providers, and relationship-based sales professionals through trusted recommendations, referrals, and shared economic opportunity.

Kinzman has an established founder, technical leadership, and a developing platform and business model. Our next stage is recruiting the founding creator community, building the operational and revenue infrastructure around them, and preparing for market launch.

We are seeking a hands-on founding Chief Operating Officer who can help turn the vision into a disciplined, fundable, and scalable organization.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a founding executive and equity-partner opportunity for an entrepreneurial operator who understands that early-stage leadership requires building before managing.

The COO will work alongside Kinzman’s executive and technical leadership while taking primary ownership of business operations, launch execution, creator recruitment, fundraising support, and organizational development.

The strongest candidate will have meaningful experience in direct selling, network marketing or MLM, affiliate commerce, creator commerce, relationship-based sales, or a closely related business model. This person must understand both the power of community-driven distribution and the importance of building an ethical, sustainable, and compliant organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Translate Kinzman’s vision and business model into clear operational priorities, timelines, and measurable goals

• Develop and execute the strategy for recruiting, onboarding, engaging, and retaining Kinzman’s founding creator community

• Build and lead the initial sales and business-development structure needed to recruit creators, establish partnerships, and generate early revenue

• Build the operational infrastructure needed to support creators, connectors, consumers, sales teams, and strategic partners

• Help develop and execute Kinzman’s fundraising strategy, including investor outreach, strategic partnerships, grant opportunities, pitch materials, and funding conversations

• Design scalable workflows, policies, performance metrics, budgets, reporting systems, and accountability structures

• Lead launch planning, early revenue strategy, resource allocation, and organizational growth

• Recruit, organize, and lead operational and revenue-producing teams as resources become available

• Collaborate closely with technical leadership to ensure the platform supports business priorities, user needs, and operational requirements

• Identify execution risks, ownership gaps, financial needs, and operational barriers before they interfere with growth

• Help build a culture grounded in accountability, transparency, collaboration, ethical leadership, and Connection Over Competition

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

• Senior leadership experience in operations, business development, fundraising, sales, or organizational growth

• Direct experience with network marketing, MLM, direct selling, affiliate marketing, creator commerce, referral-based sales, or community-led growth

• Demonstrated fundraising ability or strong relationships with investors, grantmakers, strategic partners, sponsors, or other funding sources

• Experience building or scaling an early-stage company, startup, sales organization, marketplace, or membership-based business

• Strong financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, revenue-development, and performance-management capabilities

• Ability to create structure, lead people, and execute without established corporate infrastructure

• Strong negotiation, communication, accountability, and cross-functional leadership skills

• The judgment to distinguish sustainable relationship-based commerce from exploitative or poorly structured MLM practices

• Alignment with Kinzman’s mission and willingness to protect the integrity of its people-centered business model

A specific degree is not required. Proven experience, execution ability, professional relationships, leadership judgment, and alignment with Kinzman’s mission will carry greater weight than formal credentials.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

This is a fully remote opportunity with flexible scheduling during Kinzman’s pre-funding stage. The selected candidate may maintain other professional commitments while contributing agreed time, deliverables, and leadership toward defined company milestones.

The opportunity is intended to expand into a more substantial executive commitment as Kinzman secures funding, generates sustainable revenue, and moves into active operations.

COMPENSATION

Kinzman is currently pre-revenue and pre-funding. This is a founding partnership opportunity, not a currently salaried employee position. There is no immediate salary or guaranteed cash compensation.

The selected candidate will be offered a formally negotiated founding-executive compensation structure that may include equity participation and success-contingent deferred cash compensation. Cash compensation will begin only after mutually defined funding or revenue milestones are achieved.

Equity, vesting, deferred compensation, performance expectations, decision-making authority, time commitments, milestones, and exit provisions will be documented in a written agreement following mutual due diligence and professional review.

This opportunity is best suited for an entrepreneurial executive who is financially able to contribute during the building stage and is motivated by meaningful ownership and long-term value creation. It is not appropriate for someone who requires an immediate guaranteed salary.

TO APPLY

Please submit your LinkedIn profile or résumé and briefly address the following:

• Your experience in direct selling, network marketing, MLM, affiliate commerce, creator commerce, or relationship-based sales

• An organization, program, or revenue system you helped build or scale

• Your fundraising experience and measurable results

• Your availability during the pre-funding stage

• Why a remote, flexible, equity-based founding opportunity is appropriate for you at this stage of your career
